```md docs/autonomous-agent.md
# Autonomous Agent — Feature Specification

## Overview

codx-junior introduces a powerful **Autonomous Agent** capable of handling complex feature development end-to-end. The agent follows an agile approach: it understands business requirements, investigates the codebase, plans and distributes work, implements changes in isolation, and finally submits everything through a structured review process before any file is touched in the real project.

---

## How It Works — The Full Lifecycle

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    U([User]) -->|Creates task with\nbusiness requirements| A[Autonomous Agent]
    A -->|Searches project for\nsimilar functionality| KB[(Knowledge Base)]
    A -->|Needs clarification?| U
    U -->|Adds details &\nacceptance criteria| A
    A -->|Splits work into sub-tasks\nwith assigned profiles| T[Sub-Tasks]
    T -->|Executed by\nspecialized agents| VF[(Virtual File System)]
    VF -->|Pull Request created| PR[PR Reviewer]
    PR -->|Approved| P[Real Project Files]
    PR -->|Changes needed| U
```

---

## Step-by-Step Flow

### 1. Task Creation
The user creates a task with business requirements written in plain language.

> **Example:**
> *"We need to create a performant monitoring dashboard to allow admins to see tasks."*

---

### 2. Agent Evaluation

The agent evaluates whether the requirements are sufficient to start work. It:

- **Searches the project knowledge base** (`project_search`) for similar existing functionality, patterns, and relevant components.
- **Reads related files** (`project_read_file`) to understand the current implementation context.
- **Requests clarification** from the user if the requirements are ambiguous or incomplete.

> **Key Rule:** The agent will not proceed until it has enough information to define clear, verifiable acceptance criteria.

<details>
<summary>What the agent looks for during evaluation</summary>

- Existing similar features that can be reused or extended
- Current architectural patterns (e.g., API structure, component conventions)
- Related data models or services
- Potential conflicts or dependencies with existing code

</details>

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria Definition

The user provides an **Acceptance Criteria** list. This list is the checklist used by the agent — and the PR Reviewer — to determine when the task is done.

> **Example Acceptance Criteria:**
> - Admin users can see a real-time list of all active tasks
> - Each task row displays: name, status, assigned profile, elapsed time
> - Dashboard auto-refreshes every 30 seconds
> - Non-admin users cannot access the dashboard

---

### 4. Task Splitting & Profile Assignment

Once requirements are clear, the agent splits the work into **sub-tasks** and assigns the appropriate **profile** to each one. Profiles define both the role and the tools available to the agent executing each sub-task.

> **Example Sub-Tasks Generated:**
>
> | # | Task | Profile |
> |---|------|---------|
> | Task 1 | Analyse requirements and design dashboard data model | `analyst` |
> | Task 2 | Implement backend API endpoint for task monitoring | `software_developer` |
> | Task 3 | Build frontend dashboard component | `software_developer` |
> | Task 4 | Write tests and validate acceptance criteria | `software_developer` |

#### Available Profiles

| Profile | Role | Tools Available |
|---------|------|-----------------|
| `analyst` | Clarifies and documents requirements | `project_search`, `project_read_file` |
| `software_developer` | Implements code changes | `project_search`, `project_read_file`, `apply_file_changes`, `project_write_file` |
| `browser` | Fetches external references and documentation | `fetch_webpage` |

---

### 5. Isolated Execution — Virtual File System

All file changes produced during task execution are stored in a **virtual version of the project**. No changes are applied directly to the real project files during this phase.

This ensures:
- The live project is never broken by in-progress work
- Multiple tasks can run in parallel without conflicts
- All changes can be reviewed before being applied

> **Tools used during execution:**
>
> - `project_search` — RAG search within the knowledge base
> - `project_read_file` — Read existing project files
> - `project_write_file` — Write new files to the virtual file system
> - `apply_file_changes` — Apply precise search-and-replace edits to existing files
> - `fetch_webpage` — Fetch external documentation or references
> - `generate_tasks_tool` — Further split complex tasks into sub-tasks

---

### 6. Agent Monitoring & Iteration

The agent monitors each sub-task's progress, tracking status across the following phases:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending
    Pending --> Creating : Task started
    Creating --> Done : Completed successfully
    Creating --> Error : Failed
    Done --> [*]
    Error --> Creating : Retried
```

During execution, the agent may:
- Request corrections from the user if it encounters unclear requirements
- Automatically retry failed steps within the configured iteration limit
- Signal completion with a done marker once all acceptance criteria are met

---

### 7. Pull Request Review

When all sub-tasks are complete, the agent creates a **Pull Request (PR)** containing all the virtual file changes. The PR Reviewer provides:

- A full diff of every file created, modified, or deleted
- A summary of changes mapped against the acceptance criteria checklist
- Conflict detection — if a real project file has changed since the task started, the reviewer flags it so the changes can be re-applied cleanly over the latest version

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    PR[Pull Request] --> RV{Reviewer}
    RV -->|Approved| APPLY[Apply changes\nto project]
    RV -->|Changes requested| FB[Feedback to Agent]
    RV -->|File conflict detected| REBASE[Re-apply over\nlatest version]
    FB --> PR
    REBASE --> PR
```

---

### 8. Applying Changes

Once the PR is approved, all virtual file changes are applied to the real project. The process is atomic — either all changes are applied successfully, or none are, preventing partial states.

---

## Key Concepts

### Profiles
A profile defines an agent's role, instructions, and the set of tools it can use. Profiles are assigned per sub-task to ensure the right specialist handles each piece of work.

```json
{
  "name": "software_developer",
  "description": "Implements code following best practices.",
  "tools": ["project_search", "project_read_file", "apply_file_changes"]
}
```

### Virtual File System
A sandboxed, in-memory (or temporary) copy of the project where agents write their changes. Acts as the staging area before a PR is raised.

### Acceptance Criteria Checklist
A list of verifiable conditions defined by the user before work begins. The agent uses this list to self-assess completion and the PR Reviewer uses it to validate the final output.

### Pull Request Conflict Detection
If a real project file has been modified after the task started, the PR Reviewer detects the divergence and informs the user. The agent can then re-apply its changes on top of the latest version of the file.

---

## Complete Example

**User input:**
> *"We need to create a performant monitoring dashboard to allow admins to see tasks."*

**Agent evaluation:**
> Agent searches the knowledge base — finds existing Kanban board API and chat task manager. Asks: *"Should this dashboard reuse the existing Kanban data model or be a separate view?"*

**User clarification + Acceptance Criteria:**
> *"Separate read-only view. Admins only."*
>
> Acceptance Criteria:
> - [ ] Admin-only route `/admin/tasks`
> - [ ] Real-time task list with status, name, elapsed time
> - [ ] Auto-refresh every 30 seconds
> - [ ] Unit tests for the new API endpoint

**Agent splits tasks:**
> - Task 1: Design data model and API contract (`analyst`)
> - Task 2: Implement `GET /api/admin/tasks` endpoint (`software_developer`)
> - Task 3: Build `AdminTasksDashboard` frontend component (`software_developer`)
> - Task 4: Write unit tests (`software_developer`)

**Execution:**
> All changes written to virtual file system. Agent marks task done.

**PR raised:**
> Reviewer sees 4 new/modified files, all acceptance criteria checked. Approves.

**Changes applied** to the real project. ✅
```

---

This document serves as a comprehensive guide for agents on how to effectively perform a coding task. Ensure all sections are thoroughly completed to facilitate understanding and execution.

## Task

- **Name:** Provide the name of the task.
- **Description:** Offer a concise yet comprehensive description of the task to be accomplished.

## Objectives

Clearly outline the objectives of the task. These objectives will be evaluated to confirm the task's successful completion. Ensure they are specific, measurable, and relevant to the task.

## Tests

Detail the list of tests that need to be conducted to validate the completion of the task. Each test should be described in a way that makes it easy to understand what is being tested and the expected outcome.

## Flow

Define the task flow using a mermaid diagram. This diagram should illustrate the steps the agent must follow to successfully complete the task. Ensure clarity in each step and include all necessary tools and methods available to the agent.

### Available Tools

Agents can utilize the following tools during the task:

- **search(query: str) -> List[Document]:** This function allows agents to perform a RAG (Retrieve and Generate) search within the project's knowledge base. It will return a list of documents and relevant information that agents can use to execute the task.
  
- **code(patch: str) -> bool:** This function allows agents to execute code changes. Agents must provide a file patch in the form of a diff. A boolean will be returned, indicating whether the patch was successfully applied.
